usage: This is the most common and versatile way to say "please" across the Levant, used to politely request something or get someone's attention like a waiter. It conjugates depending on the gender and number of the people you are speaking to. In Lebanon and parts of Syria, "iza bitreed" is also heavily used, while younger speakers everywhere frequently just use the English word "please".

variants.label: to a man
variants.note: The default form used when addressing a single male.

variants.label: to a woman
variants.note: Used when addressing a single female.

variants.label: to a group
variants.note: Used when addressing two or more people.

variants.label: Lebanese/Syrian alternative
variants.note: A very common alternative in Lebanon and Syria, literally meaning 'if you want'.

variants.label: more formal
variants.note: Slightly more formal, often used in customer service or professional settings.

examples.english: Please, can I have the bill?
Bring me a coffee, please (to a woman).
Please close the door (to a group).
